evidence.quote: reinforced TiB2 particles are not ideal homogeneously distribute and their clusters are often dispersed mainly along the eutectic Si at grain boundaries
Orowan strengthening effect, caused by the resistance of closely spaced hard particles to the passing of dislocations.

Coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch strengthening, a number of appending dislocations around the reinforced particles due to the residual plastic strain induced by the CTE mismatch between the reinforcement and the matrix
Load-bearing effect, the strong bonding between the dispersed particles and the matrix contributes to transfer of the load applied to the material
This will lower the probability of damage via particle cracking but increase the particle–matrix interface debonding.
Dislocation cross slip and climb are the important deformation modes of the composite at 350°C, which are induced by the high thermal activation process.
